title: Navbar
purpose: Provide consistent global navigation to the site's most important destinations while preserving orientation and operability across responsive states.

composition.role: show or hide an optional child link group
composition.semantics: button controlling a list of links

composition.role: show or hide the same navigation at narrow widths
secondary service destinations that remain navigation

layout.wide_state: home link and global navigation presented in a horizontal or otherwise immediately visible composition
layout.narrow_state: the same information architecture may collapse behind one explicit disclosure trigger
layout.hierarchy: primary and utility navigation must remain distinguishable

visual.preserve: clear hierarchy, current-state visibility and distinguishable interactive states

behavior.navigation_targets: Links navigate; buttons disclose. Do not combine both behaviors in one control.
behavior.site_navigation_role: Use normal site-navigation semantics by default; do not apply menu or menubar roles unless intentionally implementing the complete widget contract.
behavior.current_page: At most one relevant destination in the rendered navigation should expose aria-current="page".

disclosures.enabled_when: a global navigation item owns a real group of child destinations
disclosures.relationship: aria-controls when a stable controlled element id is available
disclosures.escape: When a disclosed group is open, Escape closes it and focus returns to or remains on its controlling trigger.
disclosures.arrow_keys: optional enhancement; never a replacement for normal Tab order

responsive_navigation.trigger: native button when collapse is necessary
responsive_navigation.escape: When the narrow navigation panel is open, Escape closes it and returns focus to the mobile trigger.

behavior.outside_pointer: A transient wide-screen disclosure may close on pointer interaction outside the navigation, provided keyboard behavior remains independent.

accessibility.landmark_label: Required when needed to distinguish this navigation landmark from other navigation landmarks on the page.
accessibility.current_page_state: aria-current="page" when a rendered link represents the current page
accessibility.focus_obscuring: Author-created sticky or overlay behavior must not completely obscure a focused component.
page_integration: The host page provides a bypass mechanism for repeated global navigation, commonly a skip link before the header/navigation.
If sticky positioning is enabled, test focused descendants and subsequent page controls against WCAG 2.4.11.

constraints: Do not use role="menu" or role="menubar" for ordinary website navigation unless the full widget interaction model is intentionally implemented.
Do not make a control both navigate and disclose at the same time.
Do not make child navigation hover-only.
Do not silently change labels, destinations or ordering between wide and narrow states.
Do not remove essential destinations at narrower widths; collapse them into an operable disclosure instead.
Do not invent site hierarchy or utility destinations from the visual example.
Do not treat mobile navigation as a separate content variant.
Do not expand the Navbar into a full Site Header: promotional bars, complete search systems, cart/account workflows and mega menus are separate concerns.

agent_contract.instruction: Reconstruct the Navbar from this Build DNA rather than copying reference HTML. Adapt implementation details to the target stack. Preserve the supplied information architecture and ask for missing navigation decisions instead of inventing them.
agent_contract.when_conflicting: Purpose, constraints, behavior and accessibility override visual resemblance.
agent_contract.output_expectation: Production-appropriate navigation code for the requested stack, plus explicitly listed unresolved information-architecture decisions.

request_examples.intent: Build a Navbar from the generic how-to-web contract.
request_examples.prompt: Baue mir eine Navbar nach https://blame76.github.io/how-to-web/elements/navigation/navbar/ und nutze die Build DNA als Rekonstruktionsvertrag.

request_examples.intent: Build one documented variant while keeping the generic contract normative.
request_examples.prompt: Baue mir die Variante "With Disclosures" nach der how-to-web Navbar-Referenz. Nutze die Build DNA als Vertrag und das Beispiel nur als Ausprägung.

request_examples.intent: Adapt the Navbar contract to an existing stack and design system.
request_examples.prompt: Übertrage die how-to-web Navbar in mein bestehendes Projekt. Bewahre Semantik, Responsive-, Focus- und Disclosure-Regeln; nutze vorhandene Tokens und Komponenten und erfinde fehlende IA-Entscheidungen nicht.

acceptance: Every supplied global destination is reachable as a real link.
The home/brand destination is a real link.
The current page is visibly distinguishable and programmatically exposed when supplied.
Disclosure groups use buttons with exposed expanded state and do not require hover.
Normal Tab and Shift+Tab navigation reaches all operable controls and links.
Escape closes an open disclosure or narrow navigation panel and restores logical focus.
Wide and narrow states preserve labels, destination targets and order.
No essential navigation destination disappears at narrow widths.
There is no horizontal overflow at 320 CSS px.
The navigation remains usable at 200% zoom.
Pointer targets satisfy WCAG 2.2 target-size minimum or a documented exception.
Sticky or overlay behavior does not completely obscure focused components.
The host page has a bypass mechanism for repeated navigation.

examples.note: Direct global links with a narrow disclosure state.
Global navigation with explicit disclosure groups and nested links.
Primary and utility navigation kept distinct within one Navbar organism.
